Sarah —

Appreciate the clear asks. Below is a concise, contract-friendly proposal that we can put into the SOW / SLA appendix. I've looped Priya and Diego for the technical and operational details; Evelyn from Legal will draft the final contractual clause.

Proposed SLA (summary):
- Applicability: Applies to asynchronous batch inference jobs submitted via Redwood Batch API (single job = single job_id) on Redwood Dedicated.
- Job completion windows (standard Dedicated tier):
  - P95 completion: 30 minutes per 100k requests (typical model family T)
  - P99 completion: 2 hours per 100k requests
  - For larger batches, completion windows scale linearly with batch size; will add explicit scale factor in SOW (e.g., +30 min per additional 100k requests for P95).
- Retries and failure handling:
  - Automatic retries: Redwood will attempt up to 3 retries for transient worker failures with exponential backoff starting at 30s.
  - If retries fail, job state = FAILED; Redwood will surface a failure report and a job artifact with per-request status.
- Idempotency and deduplication:
  - Customers must provide client-generated idempotency keys (job_id and optional per-item id). Redwood guarantees de-duplication based on job_id and item ids within a configurable retention window (default 72 hours).
  - Semantic guarantee: at-least-once processing for individual items; best-effort de-duplication where idempotency keys are present. Exactly-once cannot be guaranteed for arbitrary user models that have side effects.
- Remedies and credits:
  - SLA credit triggers when monthly P95 or P99 job-completion targets are not met for Dedicated capacity. Credit = pro-rated service fee for affected billing period (specific % to be negotiated; suggested: 5% for P95 miss, 10% for P99 miss).
- Exceptions and maintenance:
  - Exemptions: scheduled maintenance windows, customer misconfiguration, and force majeure.

Hi all —

Adding technical detail so OptiSearch can validate against their pipelines:

Measurement and visibility:
- Completion definition: A job is considered "complete" when all input items have a terminal status (SUCCEEDED or FAILED) and are visible in the job artifact file (per-item result list) stored in the customer's configured object store.
- Measurement points: Redwood measures job completion at our control plane time of final artifact write; we publish per-job metrics to the customer's metrics endpoint (Prometheus/Pushgateway) and ship logs to the configured log sink.

Retries and idempotency behavior:
- Retries are performed at the per-worker level and are scoped to individual item processing — failed item -> retry up to N=3 attempts. Retried items will keep the original item id to enable de-duplication on reingest.
- Job-level retries (entire job resubmission) are not automatic. If the job fails before artifact consolidation, Redwood provides a partial artifact and a recommended resume token so the customer can re-run only missing items.
- Idempotency semantics: If customer provides per-item id (UUID) and job_id, Redwood will ensure the same item_id within the same job_id is processed once (dedupe) in the artifact. Cross-job dedupe requires explicit opt-in and longer retention; this is a separate config.

Best practices we recommend for OptiSearch:
- Provide per-item UUIDs and persist job_id for replays.
- Use resume tokens for large pipelines to avoid reprocessing entire batches on partial failures.
- For side-effecting downstream work, implement compensating transactions on the downstream system if exact-once is required.

Sarah — quick operational facts from SRE perspective:

- Monitoring & alerts:
  - We emit job.duration_seconds, job.items_processed, job.failed_items_count. Alerts fire when job.duration_seconds exceeds configured threshold for the Dedicated pool serving the job_id.
  - We can set a per-customer alerting policy (pager duty/email) for jobs nearing P95 thresholds.
- Measurement caveats:
  - Time to completion includes time in queue + processing time; queued time can vary during bursts. Our SLA numbers assume Dedicated capacity sized per SOW; burst conditions can add queue time unless burst capacity is purchased.
- Idempotency and side effects:
  - For exactly-once semantics when your downstream systems have side-effects, we recommend a two-phase commit pattern or writing results to an immutable store and having downstream systems subscribe/ack before applying changes.
- Operational exceptions:
  - Emergency maintenance or hardware failures may trigger partial job loss; in that case we provide the partial artifact and a recommended re-run strategy.

Happy to sync on the alerting/observability setup to make sure your ops team gets the right signals.
